questions.question: Which ancient ruler founded the famous Pattim cult associated with the worship of Kannagi, the goddess of chastity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Senguttuvan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Senguttuvan, a famous ruler of the Chera dynasty, is credited with establishing the worship of Kannagi as the goddess of chastity, a practice known as the Pattim cult.
 
• The tradition of honoring Kannagi originates from the Tamil epic **"Silappatikaram,"** authored by Ilango Adigal, where Kannagi is celebrated for her unwavering virtue and chastity.
 
• Senguttuvan is said to have constructed a temple for Kannagi and initiated rituals to deify her, marking the beginning of the Pattim cult.
 
• He is also known for his administrative prowess and promoting Tamil culture, literature, and arts during his reign.
 
• The worship of Kannagi as a divine figure continues to hold cultural and religious significance in parts of Tamil Nadu and Kerala to this day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chera Dynasty:**

 
 
• One of the three major Tamil dynasties, alongside the Chola and Pandya dynasties, which ruled parts of South India.
 
• The Cheras were known for their maritime trade, particularly with the Roman Empire.
 
• Their reign contributed significantly to Tamil culture, art, and literature.
 
 
 
• **Silappatikaram:**
 
 
• An ancient Tamil epic written by Ilango Adigal, revolving around the life of Kannagi and Kovalan.
 
• The epic highlights the themes of morality, justice, and the consequences of human actions.
 
• It is considered one of the finest works in Tamil literature and a treasure of Sangam poetry.
 
 
 
• **Pattim Cult:**
 
 
• The term "Pattim" refers to the worship of Kannagi as the goddess of chastity and marital virtue.
 
• This cult underscores the values of fidelity and justice as exemplified by Kannagi's life.
 
 
 
• **Kannagi's Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Kannagi is regarded as a symbol of Tamil womanhood and the epitome of chastity and patience.
 
• Her story has been immortalized not just in literature but also in temple sculptures and folk traditions.
 
• Temples dedicated to Kannagi can be found in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, where she is worshipped as a goddess.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a part of four noble truths in Buddhism?

I. Dukkha

II. Samudaya

III. Nirodha
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II, and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dukkha:** This is the first noble truth and refers to the universal nature of suffering and dissatisfaction experienced by all beings.
 
• **Samudaya:** The second noble truth identifies craving or desire (tanha) as the root cause of suffering.
 
• **Nirodha:** The third noble truth asserts that it is possible to end suffering by eliminating its causes, leading to liberation or Nirvana.
 
• The Four Noble Truths are the fundamental teachings of Buddhism, introduced by Gautama Buddha during his first sermon at Sarnath.
 
• The fourth noble truth, Magga, prescribes the Eightfold Path as a practical guide to overcome suffering and achieve enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dukkha:**

 
 
• Suffering is not limited to physical pain but includes emotional distress, dissatisfaction, and the impermanent nature of worldly pleasures.
 
• Buddha highlighted that all aspects of life, even those considered pleasurable, are subject to change and thus lead to dissatisfaction.
 
 
 
• **Samudaya:**
 
 
• This truth explains that the root of suffering lies in craving (tanha), which leads to attachment and clinging to impermanent things.
 
• Ignorance (avijja) of the true nature of reality further perpetuates the cycle of suffering.
 
 
 
• **Nirodha:**
 
 
• Also known as the cessation of suffering, it emphasizes the possibility of breaking free from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth (samsara).
 
• This state of liberation is referred to as Nirvana, a condition of ultimate peace and freedom from craving.
 
 
 
• **Magga:**
 
 
• The Eightfold Path includes ethical conduct, mental discipline, and wisdom as a practical approach to eliminate suffering.
 
• It is divided into three categories: Sila (morality), Samadhi (concentration), and Prajna (wisdom).

questions.question: Who among the following kings became the follower of the Jainism towards the later stages of his life?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the Maurya Empire in ancient India.
 
• He ruled from around 321 BCE to 297 BCE and established one of the largest empires on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• In his later years, Chandragupta Maurya became a follower of Jainism and abdicated his throne in favor of his son, Bindusara.
 
• According to Jain tradition, he migrated south to Karnataka and spent his last years as an ascetic at Shravanabelagola.
 
• He is said to have observed Sallekhana, a Jain practice of fasting to death, and passed away at Shravanabelagola.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jainism**

 
 
• Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that prescribes a path of non-violence towards all living beings.
 
• It emphasizes spiritual independence and equality between all forms of life.
 
• Jain monks and nuns strictly follow asceticism and live a life of celibacy and detachment.
 
• One of the key principles of Jainism is Ahimsa (non-violence).
 
 
 
• **Sallekhana**
 
 
• Sallekhana is a Jain ritual of voluntary fasting to death, observed by a person who feels that their life is nearing its end.
 
• It is considered a peaceful and dignified way to end one's life by reducing passions and desires.
 
• The practice is seen as a way to purify the soul and achieve spiritual liberation (Moksha).
 
 
 
• **Maurya Empire**
 
 
• The Maurya Empire was established by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE.
 
• It became one of the largest and most powerful empires in ancient India.
 
• The empire's capital was Pataliputra (modern-day Patna).
 
• It reached its peak under the rule of Ashoka, Chandragupta's grandson.
 
 
 
• **Shravanabelagola**
 
 
• Shravanabelagola is a significant Jain pilgrimage site located in the state of Karnataka, India.
 
• It is home to the famous statue of Gommateshwara Bahubali, one of the largest free-standing monolithic statues in the world.
 
• The site is associated with the final days of Chandragupta Maurya, who is believed to have taken Sallekhana here.

questions.question: In the reference of the Delhi Sultanate, what was the 'Group of Forty'?

options.text: They were mostly powerful Turkish slaves of Iltutmish, who took power in the interregnum following Sultana Raziyya's killing.
They were forty military archers who distinguished themselves by their bravery in the Delhi Sultanate.
They were forty banjara leaders who transferred military supplies in times of war.
They were forty Rajput nobles who planned a coup to dethrone Qutb ud Din Aibak in 1210.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'Group of Forty' or 'Chihalgani'** was a significant political faction in the **Delhi Sultanate during the 13th century. **
 
• This group was **primarily composed of forty powerful Turkish nobles** and slaves who were closely associated with Sultan Iltutmish (reigned 1211-1236)
 
• This group was responsible for** various critical roles in the military, administration, and governance.**
 
• After **the death of Iltutmish in 1236,** the Chihalgani became very powerful, exerting substantial influence over the succession and governance of the Sultanate. 
 
• Iltutmish, daughter Raziyya Sultan ascended to the throne but her reign faced strong opposition, particularly from the Chihalgani

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iltutmish (Reigned 1211-1236)**

 
 
• Iltutmish was originally a **slave of Qutb-ud-din Aibak,** the founder of the Mamluk Dynasty.
 
• He became **Sultan of Delhi after defeating Aram Shah,** a rival claimant, thereby solidifying his position as the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Iltutmish is **credited with consolidating and centralizing the administration of the Delhi Sultanate,** setting up an efficient governance structure.
 
• He** introduced the iqta system**, where land was granted to military commanders in exchange for their services.
 
 
 
• **Razia Sultan (Reigned 1236-1240)**
 
 
• **​**Razia Sultan was **the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate**, breaking significant gender barriers in the Muslim world.
 
• **Nominated by her father Iltutmish**, she overcame initial resistance from the nobility to ascend to the throne.
 
• Razia was **known for her competent administration**, showing a commitment to justice and effective governance.

questions.question:
Pick the two right combinations from the list given below:

1. Rathod - Jodhpur

2. Sisodia - Udaipur

3. Qaranah Turks - Jaunpur

4. Malik Kafur-Awadh

5. Karni Mata Temple - Jaipur

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - 1, 2 Only**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **1. Rathod - Jodhpur**

 
 
• The Rathod (or Rathore) clan is historically associated with the region of Jodhpur in Rajasthan.
 
• The Rathore dynasty established and ruled the kingdom of Marwar, with Jodhpur as its capital.
 
• Jodhpur is often called the "Sun City" due to its bright and sunny weather throughout the year.
 
 
 
• **2. Sisodia - Udaipur**
 
 
• The Sisodia clan is historically linked to the region of Udaipur in Rajasthan.
 
• The Sisodia dynasty founded and ruled the kingdom of Mewar, with Udaipur as its capital.
 
• Udaipur is renowned for its palaces, lakes, and rich cultural heritage, and is often referred to as the "City of Lakes."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **3. Qaranah Turks - Jaunpur**

 
 
• The Qaranah Turks are not specifically associated with Jaunpur in historical records.
 
• Jaunpur was founded by the Sultan of Delhi, Feroz Shah Tughlaq, and later ruled by the Sharqi dynasty.
 
 
 
• **4. Malik Kafur - Awadh**
 
 
• Malik Kafur was a prominent general of Alauddin Khilji of the Delhi Sultanate and is not specifically linked to Awadh.
 
• Awadh (or Oudh) was a region in northern India, which later became a princely state and was ruled by the Nawabs of Awadh.
 
 
 
• **5. Karni Mata Temple - Jaipur**
 
 
• Karni Mata Temple is actually located in Deshnoke, near Bikaner, not Jaipur.
 
• Karni Mata is revered as an incarnation of the goddess Durga, and the temple is famous for its sacred rats.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution deals with Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 16** of the Indian Constitution guarantees **equality of opportunity in matters of public employment**.
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, or any of them.
 
• It ensures that no citizen shall be discriminated against or be ineligible for any employment or office under the State on these grounds.
 
• Article 16 complements Article 14, which provides for equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This article is a fundamental right and is enforceable by the courts under the judicial review system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14**

 
 
• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution provides for **equality before the law** and equal protection of the laws.
 
• It ensures that individuals in similar situations are treated equally by the law.
 
• The principle of equality is a fundamental aspect of the Rule of Law in India.
 
 
 
• **Article 15**
 
 
• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• This article also allows the state to make special provisions for women and children and for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Article 17**
 
 
• Article 17 abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• The enforcement of any disability arising out of "untouchability" shall be an offense punishable in accordance with the law.
 
 
 
• **Article 18**
 
 
• Article 18 abolishes titles except for military and academic distinctions.
 
• It prohibits the state from conferring any title upon any citizen or foreigner.
 
• Citizens of India are also prohibited from accepting any title from any foreign state.

questions.question: As per Article ________ of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**75(3)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per Article **75(3)** of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
• This implies that the entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is accountable to the Lok Sabha for its actions and policies.
 
• If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no confidence against the Council of Ministers, they must collectively resign.
 
• This collective responsibility ensures that the executive branch of the government is answerable to the legislative branch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of collective responsibility is fundamental to the parliamentary system of government.
 
• It ensures that the executive remains responsible and accountable to the legislature, and through it, to the people.
 
• This principle is essential for maintaining the stability and integrity of the government.
 
• Article 75 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibilities of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• Article 75(1) states that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President, and the other ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• Article 75(2) mentions that the ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• Article 75(3) establishes the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which feature of the Preamble of the Constitution is highlighted by 'Elected President' ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Republic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'Republic' in the Preamble indicates that the head of state is elected and not a hereditary monarch.
 
• In a Republic, the supreme power lies with the people and their elected representatives.
 
• Article 52 of the Indian Constitution establishes the office of the President of India, who is elected.
 
• This ensures that the highest public office in the country is accessible to any eligible citizen, promoting equality and democratic values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sovereign:**

 
 
• The term 'Sovereign' means that India is a fully independent country and not subject to the control of any other state or external authority.
 
• It signifies the supreme power of the Indian state to make laws and govern itself.
 
 
 
• **Secular:**
 
 
• The term 'Secular' means that the state treats all religions impartially and does not endorse or favor any religion.
 
• It ensures freedom of religion and the state's neutrality in religious matters.
 
 
 
• **Socialist:**
 
 
• The term 'Socialist' in the Preamble reflects the commitment to social and economic equality.
 
• It aims to reduce income inequality and ensure a fair distribution of wealth.
 
 
 
• **Democratic:**
 
 
• The term 'Democratic' indicates that India has a system of government where the power is vested in the hands of the people.
 
• It emphasizes the principles of free and fair elections, and the rule of law.

questions.question: ________ is defined as excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings during a fiscal year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal deficit.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is the difference between a government's total expenditure and its total revenue, excluding any borrowing, within a specific fiscal year.
 
• **Formula**
 
 
• Fiscal Deficit=**Total Expenditure−(Total Revenue+Non-Debt Receipts)**
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Economy**:
 
 
• **Inflation**: Persistent fiscal deficits can lead to higher inflation if funded by printing more money.
 
• **Interest Rates**: Higher fiscal deficits can lead to increased borrowing costs as the government competes for funds in the financial markets.
 
• **Public Debt**: A high fiscal deficit adds to the government’s debt burden, potentially leading to higher interest payments in the future.
 
 
 
• **Policy Measures**
 
 
• **Increase Revenue**: Through higher taxes or better tax compliance.
 
• **Reduce Expenditure**: By cutting down on non-essential spending.
 
• **Borrow Responsibly**: Managing debt to ensure it does not become unsustainable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Type of Deficit
 Definition
 
 
 
 

 Income Deficit
 The shortfall between total government revenue and total government expenditure.
 
 

 Structural Deficit
 The part of the fiscal deficit that arises from structural imbalances in the economy and budgetary policies.
 
 

 Gross Primary Deficit
 The fiscal deficit before accounting for interest payments on previous borrowings.

questions.question: If the value/percentage of the cash reserve ratio falls, then the value of money multiplier ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rises**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **money multiplier** represents how much the money supply in the economy can increase with a given increase in bank reserves.
 
• A **lower CRR** means that banks are required to keep less cash in reserves, **allowing them to lend more money**.
 
• As banks lend more, **the creation of money in the economy increases**, thus** raising the value of the money multiplier.**
 
• In addition, when the CRR decreases, banks have more funds available for lending, this increase in lending further amplifies the money supply, thereby **enhancing the overall liquidity in the financial system.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 **Repo Rate**

 The rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks, typically to control inflation.
 
 

 **Reverse Repo Rate**

 The rate at which banks park surplus funds with the RBI, helps to absorb liquidity.
 
 

 **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**

 The percentage of total deposits banks must keep as reserves with the RBI.

 The percentage of net demand and time liabilities that banks must hold in the form of gold or government securities.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the Badminton game and match length?

options.text: A match consists of the best of four games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of two games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of five games of 21 points.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A match in badminton consists of the best of three games of 21 points.
 
• The first player or pair to reach 21 points wins the game, provided there is a minimum lead of 2 points.
 
• If the score reaches 20-20, the game continues until one player or pair gains a 2-point lead (e.g., 22-20, 23-21).
 
• If the score reaches 29-29, the first player or pair to reach 30 points wins the game.
 
• The winner of a match is the first to win two games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).
 
• The sport can be played in singles (one player per side) or doubles (two players per side).
 
• Badminton became an Olympic sport in 1992 at the Barcelona Games.
 
• The court dimensions for singles and doubles are different, with the doubles court being wider.
 
• Players must serve diagonally across the court to their opponent.
 
• The serve must be underhand and the shuttlecock must be hit below the server's waist.

questions.question: Ali-Aye-Ligang, the spring festival, is observed on the first Wednesday of the Phagun month in the Indian state of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ali-Aye-Ligang is a significant spring festival celebrated by the Mising community in Assam.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the sowing season and is held on the first Wednesday of the Phagun month (February-March).
 
• The name "Ali-Aye-Ligang" translates to "sowing of seeds" in the Mising language.
 
• During the festival, traditional dances, music, and feasts are organized to celebrate the agricultural cycle.
 
• It is an important cultural event that emphasizes the agrarian lifestyle and traditions of the Mising tribe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mising Tribe**

 
 
• The Mising are one of the largest ethnic groups in Assam.
 
• They are primarily agrarian and have a rich cultural heritage with distinct traditions and rituals.
 
• Their traditional attire includes the "Mekhela Sador" for women and "Dhoti" and "Gamosa" for men.
 
 
 
• **Phagun Month**
 
 
• Phagun is the twelfth month of the Hindu calendar, corresponding to February-March in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It marks the end of winter and the beginning of the spring season.
 
• Several Indian festivals, including Holi, are celebrated during this month.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Festivals in India**
 
 
• India, being an agrarian country, celebrates various agricultural festivals such as Baisakhi, Pongal, and Makar Sankranti.
 
• These festivals are region-specific and mark important phases in the agricultural cycle.
 
• They often involve rituals, dances, and community feasts to invoke blessings for a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Dances of Assam**
 
 
• Assam has a rich tradition of folk dances, including Bihu, Bagurumba, and Sattriya.
 
• Bihu dance is performed during the Bihu festival, celebrating the Assamese New Year and the farming season.
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form that originated from the Vaishnavite monasteries of Assam.

questions.question: Which state government started the 'Shantala Natya Sri Award' in 1995 in the field of classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shantala Natya Sri Award** was initiated by the **Karnataka State Government** in **1995**.
 
• This award is dedicated to the field of **classical dance** and is named after **Queen Shantala**, who was a renowned patron of art and culture.
 
• Queen Shantala was the wife of **King Vishnuvardhana** of the **Hoysala dynasty** and was known for her exceptional contributions to the promotion of art forms, especially dance.
 
• The award aims to honor and recognize excellence in the domain of **Indian classical dance**, which includes forms like **Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, and Odissi**.
 
• Karnataka has a rich cultural heritage and a strong connection to classical art forms, making it an ideal state to institute such an award.
 
• The **Shantala Natya Sri Award** is one of the most prestigious recognitions in the field of dance and serves as a motivation for artists to preserve and promote traditional Indian dance forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __

 __

• **Tamil Nadu**__

questions.question: The Indian Statue of Unity is located near:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Sarovar Dam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Statue of Unity, which is a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is located near the Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat, India.
 
• It is the world's tallest statue, standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet).
 
• The statue was inaugurated on October 31, 2018, by the Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi, on the 143rd birth anniversary of Sardar Patel.
 
• The Statue of Unity aims to inspire citizens through the life and contributions of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who played a significant role in the integration of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Sarovar Dam**

 
 
• The Sardar Sarovar Dam is a gravity dam on the Narmada river near Navagam, Gujarat in India.
 
• It is part of the Narmada Valley Project, a large hydraulic engineering project involving the construction of a series of large irrigation and hydroelectric multi-purpose dams on the Narmada River.
 
• The dam provides water for drinking, irrigation, and hydroelectric power generation to the states of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.
 
• The project has been a subject of controversy due to its environmental and human impacts, particularly concerning the displacement of local communities.
 
 
 
• **Hirakud Dam**
 
 
• Hirakud Dam is built across the Mahanadi River, about 15 kilometers from Sambalpur in Odisha, India.
 
• It is one of the longest dams in the world, with a total length of about 25.8 kilometers including dykes.
 
• The dam is used for flood control, irrigation, and power generation.
 
 
 
• **Tehri Dam**
 
 
• Tehri Dam is a multi-purpose rock and earth-fill embankment dam on the Bhagirathi River near Tehri in Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It is the tallest dam in India and one of the tallest in the world.
 
• The primary purpose of the dam is to provide water for irrigation, municipal water supply, and the generation of hydroelectricity.
 
 
 
• **Bhakra-Nangal Dam**
 
 
• Bhakra-Nangal Dam is a concrete gravity dam on the Sutlej River in Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• The dam forms the Gobind Sagar reservoir, providing water for irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• It is one of the highest gravity dams in the world and the second largest dam in Asia.

questions.question: In an ecosystem, physical factors like temperature, rainfall, wind, soil and minerals are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**abiotic components**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Abiotic components** refer to the non-living physical and chemical elements in an ecosystem.
 
• These components include factors such as **temperature, rainfall, wind, soil, and minerals**.
 
• Abiotic factors significantly influence the types of organisms that can live in an ecosystem and their distribution.
 
• Examples of abiotic components also include sunlight, water, air, and nutrients.
 
• Abiotic components interact with biotic components (living organisms) to create a balanced ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biotic Components**:

 
 
• Biotic components are the living organisms in an ecosystem, such as plants, animals, fungi, and microorganisms.
 
• They interact with abiotic components to sustain life and maintain ecological balance.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers**:
 
 
• Decomposers are organisms like bacteria and fungi that break down dead organic matter, returning nutrients to the soil.
 
• They play a crucial role in nutrient cycling within ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Abiotic Factors**:
 
 
• Abiotic factors determine the physical environment in which biotic components live.
 
• They influence growth rates, reproductive success, and survival of organisms.
 
 
 
• **Interaction of Abiotic and Biotic Factors**:
 
 
• Both sets of components interact to create a dynamic and functional ecosystem.
 
• Changes in abiotic factors can lead to shifts in the types of biotic communities present.

questions.question: All information from our environment is detected by the specialised tips of some nerve cells and these receptors are usually located in our sense organs such as:

options.text: the inner ear, the nose and the tongue

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the inner ear, the nose and the tongue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Our sense organs contain specialized receptors that detect information from the environment.
 
• The primary sense organs include the inner ear, nose, and tongue, which are equipped with different types of receptors.
 
• The inner ear contains mechanoreceptors that detect sound and balance.
 
• The nose contains olfactory receptors that detect smell.
 
• The tongue contains taste receptors that detect different tastes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Receptors**

 
 
• Receptors are specialized structures that respond to specific stimuli from the environment.
 
• Different receptors are found in various sense organs, each tuned to specific types of stimuli.
 
 
 
• **Mechanoreceptors**
 
 
• These receptors respond to mechanical stimuli such as touch, pressure, and sound.
 
• Found primarily in the skin and the inner ear.
 
 
 
• **Olfactory Receptors**
 
 
• These receptors are responsible for the sense of smell.
 
• Located in the nasal cavity and detect airborne chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Taste Receptors**
 
 
• These receptors detect different tastes such as sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami.
 
• Located on the taste buds of the tongue.

questions.question: Which polyatomic ionic compound is a white, crystalline powder used in fire extinguishers and to neutralise acids and bases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium Bicarbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium bicarbonate, commonly known as baking soda, is a white crystalline powder that is often used as a leavening agent in baking.
 
• It is widely used in fire extinguishers due to its ability to produce carbon dioxide when heated, which helps to suffocate fires.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate can neutralize acids and bases, making it a useful compound in various chemical reactions and for pH control.
 
• It is also used in medical applications, for instance, to treat acid indigestion and heartburn by neutralizing stomach acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium Bisulphite:**

 
 
• Sodium bisulphite (NaHSO3) is a chemical compound commonly used as a food preservative and in the treatment of wastewater.
 
• It has reducing properties and is used in various industrial applications to prevent oxidation.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Thiosulphate:**
 
 
• Sodium thiosulphate (Na2S2O3) is an inorganic compound used in photographic processing, gold extraction, and medical treatment of cyanide poisoning.
 
• It is also used in water treatment to dechlorinate water before disposal or reuse.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Chromate:**
 
 
• Sodium chromate (Na2CrO4) is a chemical compound used in the manufacture of pigments, coatings, and other industrial applications.
 
• It is highly toxic and carcinogenic, and its use is regulated due to environmental and health concerns.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate:**
 
 
• Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) is a versatile compound with applications in baking, cleaning, fire extinguishing, and medical treatments.
 
• It is a mild base that can neutralize acids and is used in various household and industrial applications.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnesium (Mg) is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid compared to aluminum (Al), zinc (Zn), and iron (Fe).
 
• When magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, it produces hydrogen gas and forms magnesium chloride:
 
• {Mg} + 2{HCl} rightarrow {MgCl}₂ + {H}₂ 
 
• This reaction is faster and more vigorous than the reactions of Al, Zn, and Fe with dilute hydrochloric acid.
 
• Magnesium is higher in the reactivity series compared to aluminum, zinc, and iron, making it more reactive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a series of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• It helps to predict how metals will react with acids, water, and other substances.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas Test**
 
 
• Hydrogen gas can be tested by bringing a lit splint near the mouth of the test tube; a 'pop' sound confirms the presence of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Reactions of Other Metals**
 
 
• Aluminum reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form aluminum chloride and hydrogen gas, but it is less vigorous due to the formation of a protective oxide layer.
 
• Zinc reacts more readily than iron but less than magnesium, forming zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
 
• Iron reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas, but the reaction is slower compared to magnesium and zinc.

questions.question: Light travels in vacuum or air, a distance of nearly __________ metres in one second.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**299,792,458 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **speed of light** in vacuum is approximately **299,792,458 metres per second (m/s)**.
 
• This constant is denoted by the symbol **c** in physics.
 
• The speed of light is fundamental in many areas of physics, particularly in the theory of **relativity**.
 
• Albert Einstein's theory of relativity relies on the speed of light as a constant, which helps in explaining the relationship between **space and time**.
 
• The speed of light is also crucial in calculating distances in astronomy, such as the distance light travels in a year, known as a **light-year**.
 
• In materials other than vacuum, such as air or glass, light travels at different speeds, but the vacuum speed remains a universal constant.
 
• This value is also used in the definition of the metre, which is the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding the speed of light has been essential in the development of technologies such as **GPS, optical fibers**, and **high-speed communication systems**.
 
• In **quantum mechanics**, the speed of light plays a key role in the equations that describe the behavior of particles at the quantum level.

questions.question: In an electrical circuit, the ammeter reading decreases to _______ when the length of the wire is doubled.

• **Current and Resistance:** According to **Ohm’s Law**, for a constant voltage, if resistance doubles, the current is halved.
 
• **Practical Impact:** In a practical circuit, this means that if you **double** the length of the wire, the increased resistance will result in less current flowing through the circuit.
 
• **Ammeter Impact:** Since the current is halved, the ammeter reading will show a value that is half of the original reading before the wire was lengthened.
